questions.text: In Laravel, what does "validation" refer to?
options: Encrypting user passwords before they are stored
Compiling Blade templates into plain PHP
Checking that user input follows specific rules before it is saved or processed further
Caching routes for faster load times
questions.explanation: Validation checks that the input data provided by users adheres to specific rules before saving it to the database or processing it further.

questions.text: What is the most common way to validate incoming data in Laravel?
options: Calling the validate method available on all incoming HTTP requests
Writing manual if checks inside the Blade view
Adding rules to routes/web.php
Running php artisan validate
questions.explanation: It is most common to use the validate method available on all incoming HTTP requests.

questions.text: The validate method is provided by which object?
options: Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route
Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model
Illuminate\View\View
Illuminate\Http\Request
questions.explanation: The validate method is provided by the Illuminate\Http\Request object.

questions.text: What happens when the rules passed to $request->validate() fail?
options: The code keeps executing normally and the invalid data is saved
An Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException is thrown and the proper error response is automatically sent back to the user
The application crashes with a blank page
The request is silently discarded and nothing is returned
questions.explanation: If the rules pass, execution continues normally. If they fail, an Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException is thrown and the proper error response is sent back to the user automatically.

questions.text: In the rule string below, what does unique:posts check?
options: That the title has no repeated characters
That only one title field is sent in the request
That the title does not already exist in the posts database table
That the title is stored in a separate posts folder
questions.explanation: unique:posts makes sure the value doesn't already exist in the posts table. (The slides use this rule in their examples without describing it; this is its standard meaning.)

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT one of the benefits of Laravel validation listed in the module?
options: Prevents invalid data from being processed or saved in the database
Enhances user experience with detailed, specific error messages
Keeps code organized by separating validation from business logic
Automatically encrypts every field before it is saved
questions.explanation: The listed benefits are: preventing invalid data, simplifying validation logic with built-in and customizable rules, better error messages, and separating validation from business logic. Encryption is not a validation feature.

questions.text: Besides a single |-delimited string, how else can validation rules be written?
options: As an array of rules, e.g. ['required', 'unique:posts', 'max:255']
As a comma-separated string, e.g. 'required, unique:posts, max:255'
As a JSON file in the config folder
As HTML attributes on the form input
questions.explanation: Validation rules may be given as arrays of rules instead of a single |-delimited string.

questions.text: What does the required rule ensure?
options: The field is a string
The field matches another field
The field is at least 1 character long only if it is present
The field is present and not empty
questions.explanation: required ensures the field is present and not empty.

questions.text: What does 'phone_number' => 'required|digits:10' check?
options: The phone number is at most 10 characters long
The phone number is numeric and exactly 10 digits long
The phone number is greater than 10
The phone number has between 1 and 10 digits
questions.explanation: digits checks that the field is an exact number of digits — here, exactly 10.

questions.text: What does the nullable rule do?
options: Forces the field to always be null
Removes the field from the request
Allows the field to be null, but still validates it if a value is provided
Skips all other rules on the field, even when a value is given
questions.explanation: nullable allows the field to be null, but it is still validated if a value is provided (e.g. 'middle_name' => 'nullable|string|max:50').

questions.text: With 'password' => 'required|confirmed', which other field must be sent with a matching value?
options: password_confirmation
confirm_password
password_repeat
confirmed_password
questions.explanation: confirmed checks that a matching {field}_confirmation field exists, so for password it's password_confirmation.

questions.text: Which rule makes sure a checkbox such as "I agree to the terms of service" has been ticked?
options: confirmed
same
required
accepted
questions.explanation: accepted ensures the field is accepted, like for terms of service (e.g. 'terms' => 'required|accepted'). required alone would not reject an unticked value such as "0" or "no".

questions.text: What does adding bail to an attribute's rules do?
options: Makes the field optional
Stops running the remaining rules on that attribute after the first validation failure
Skips validation entirely for that attribute
Redirects the user to the home page on failure
questions.explanation: bail stops running validation rules on an attribute after its first failure.

questions.text: When validation fails during a normal form submission, what does Laravel do automatically?
options: Shows a 404 page
Deletes the user's session
Redirects the user back to their previous location and flashes the errors and request input to the session
Emails the errors to the developer
questions.explanation: Laravel redirects the user back to the previous location, and all validation errors and request input are flashed to the session.

questions.text: Which variable holding the validation errors is shared with all of your application's views?
options: $errors
$validation
$messages
$failed
questions.explanation: An $errors variable is shared with all of your application's views.

questions.text: Match each validation rule to what it checks.
allChoices: The field's value is different from another field's value
The field's length falls within a range of digits
The field meets a minimum value or character length
The field matches a regular expression pattern
The field has the same value as another field

pairs.match: The field meets a minimum value or character length
The field's length falls within a range of digits
The field matches a regular expression pattern
The field has the same value as another field
The field's value is different from another field's value

questions.explanation: min: minimum value/length ('password' => 'required|min:8'). numeric: numeric value ('price'). digits_between: digit count within a range ('code' => 'digits_between:5,8'). regex: matches a pattern. same: equals another field (same:password_confirmation). different: differs from another field ('new_password' => 'different:old_password').
